1287.text:
Assertion : Electromagnetic waves with frequencies smaller than the critical frequency of ionosphere are used for communication using sky wave propagation.

1978.subject: Zoology
1978.text: Oxygen binding to haemoglobin in blood is
options: directly proportional to the concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in the medium
inversely proportional to the concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in the medium
directly proportional to the concentration of $\mathrm{CO}$ in the medium
independent of the concentration of $\mathrm{CO}$ in the medium.
1978.sol: Bohr's effect is the phenomenon whereby the affinity of the respiratory pigment i.e., haemoglobin in the blood for oxygen is reduced when the level of carbon dioxide is increased. An increase in carbon dioxide concentration makes the blood more acidic which results in decrease in the efficiency of the uptake of oxygen by haemoglobin molecules. This facilitates gaseous exchange, because more oxygen is released in the tissues where the amount of carbon dioxide is rising due to metabolic activity. In its reverse, more oxygen is taken up at the lungs where the amount of carbon dioxide is low.

4397.subject: Chemistry
4397.text: Which of the following species acts as both bronsted acid and base?
4397.sol:
A Bronsted-Lowry acid is a proton $\left(\mathrm{H}^{+}\right.$ion) donor while Bronsted-Lowry base is a proton $\left(\mathrm{H}^{+}\right.$ ion) acceptor.
$\mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+\mathrm{OH}^{-}$(Bronsted based)
$\mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+} \quad$ (Bronsted acid)
$\mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}$act as a conjugate base of sulphuric acid and does not give $\mathrm{H}^{+} . \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$ is a conjugate base of $\mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}$ and does not get ionised further. Thus, $\mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}$is Bronsted acid as well as Bronsted base.

9344.text: If \(f(x)\) is a polynomial of the second degree in \(x\) such that \(f(0)=f(1)=3, f(2)=-3\). Then, \($\int \frac{f(x)}{x^3-1}$d x=\)

\(f(0)=f(1)=3 f(2)=-3\)
Let \(f(x)=a x^2+b x+c\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad c=-3, a+b+c=-3 \Rightarrow(a+b=0) \\
& \text{and } \quad4 a+2 b+c=-1 \Rightarrow 4 a+2 b=2

a & =1, b=-1 \\

\end{aligned}\)
On comparing \(A+B=1, A-B+C=-1, A-C=-3\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad A=-1, B=2, C=2 \\

\Rightarrow & 2 l m=0 \\

\Rightarrow & n=-m $\text{ or }$n=-l \\
\because & l²+m²+n²=l $\text{ and }$l^2+m²+n²=1 \\
& 0+m²+m²=l $\text{ and }$l^2+l²=1
\end{array}

\Rightarrow & \frac{\alpha-\beta}{2} =n \pi
\end{aligned}\)
\(\Rightarrow \alpha-\beta=2 n \pi, n \in\) Integer

14196.text:
Assertion (A) The colour of radiation does not change on passing through different media.
Reason (R) The media do not absorb or emit colours.
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is a correct explanation for $A$.
Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true but $\mathrm{R}$ is not a correct explanation for $\mathrm{A}$.
A is false but $R$ is true.
14196.sol:
The colour of radiation does not change on passing through different media. This is because, when light radiation passes through different media, only wavelength and speed changes, but frequency remains same and colour of light radiation depends only on frequency.
Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
"The media do not absorb or emit colours" this statement is wrong. Because the absorption or emission of colours of radiation depends only on the nature of medium.
Hence, Reason is false.

\Rightarrow \quad & E_1-E_2=h c\left(\frac{1}{\lambda_1}-\frac{1}{\lambda_2}\right)\\
\Rightarrow \quad & E_1-E_2=h c\left(\frac{\lambda_2-\lambda_1}{\lambda_1 \lambda_2}\right)\\
\Rightarrow \quad h c= & \frac{\left(E_1-E_2\right) \lambda_1 \lambda_2}{\left(\lambda_2-\lambda_1\right)}
\end{aligned}$

&

19435.text: Two sources of sound $A$ and $B$ are moving towards and away from a stationary observer with the same speed respectively. If the frequency of the sound produced by both the sources is equal to $400$ Hz, then the speed of sources (approximately) if the observer detects 4 beats per second, is [Given, speed of sound $= 340ms^{- 1}$]
19435.sol:
Given, frequency of sound produced by sources $A$~and $B$,~${f}_{A} = {f}_{B} = 400Hz$

Speed of sound in air, $v = 340ms^{- 1}$

Apparent frequency heard by the observer when source $A$ is moving towards him,

${f}_A^{'} = \dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{S}} \times {f}_{A} = \dfrac{340}{340 - {v}_{S}} \times 400$

Apparent frequency heard by the observer when source $B$ is moving away from him,

${f}_B^{'} = \dfrac{v}{v + {v}_{s}} \times {f}_{B} = \dfrac{340}{340 + {v}_{s}} \times 400$

Given, Beats~$= {f}_A^{'} - {f}_B^{'} = 4$

$\dfrac{340}{340 - {v}_{s}} \times 400 - \dfrac{340}{340 + {v}_{s}} \times 400 = 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{34000 \times 2{v}_{S}}{{340}^{2} - {v}_S^{2}} = 1$

$\dfrac{34000 \times 2{v}_{S}}{3402} = 1$~ & $\left[∵ {v}_S^{2} < < {340}^{2}\right]$

$⇒ {v}_{s} = 1 . 7ms^{- 1}$

20072.text:
Match the metals in Column II with their characteristic properties given in Column I. $
PropertiesMetals
ALanthanoid with low value of 3^{rd } ionisation enthalpy.PV
Bf-Block element with electronic configuration [Rn]6 d^2 7 s^2QG d
C3 d -series metal whose M^{3+}{ }_{(aq)} is colourless.RT h

20072.sol:
A: Gadolinium (Gd) has the electronic configuration $[Xe] 4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$. The removal of the third electron from the $5d$ orbital is relatively easy because it results in a stable half-filled $4f^7$ configuration. Thus, Gd has a low third ionisation enthalpy. So, A = Q.

B: Thorium (Th) is an actinoid with the electronic configuration $[Rn] 6d^2 7s^2$. So, B = R.

C: Scandium (Sc) is a $3d$-series metal with the electronic configuration $[Ar] 3d^1 4s^2$. Its $Sc^{3+}$ ion has the configuration $[Ar]$, which has no $d$-electrons (d^0$). Therefore, $Sc^{3+}_{(aq)}$ is colourless. So, C = S.

D: Vanadium (V) is a 3d$-series metal. Among the given choices, Vanadium has a high enthalpy of atomisation due to the presence of unpaired electrons in the $d$-orbitals, which contribute to strong metallic bonding. So, D = P.

Combining these, we get A = Q, B = R, C = S, D = P.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{Q}$ \quad $\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R}$ \quad $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{S}$ \quad $\mathrm{D}=\mathrm{P}$

The reaction sequence is as follows:

Step [A]: Ethylene (C_2H_4$) reacts with $Br_2/CCl_4$ to form 1,2-dibromoethane (CH_2Br-CH_2Br$).

Step [B]: 1,2-dibromoethane undergoes dehydrohalogenation using alcoholic $KOH$ to form vinyl bromide (CH_2=CH-Br$).

Step [C]: Vinyl bromide is treated with $NaNH_2$ (a strong base) to undergo further dehydrohalogenation to form acetylene (C_2H_2$).

Step [D]: Acetylene undergoes cyclic polymerization when passed through a red hot iron (Fe) tube to form benzene (C_6H_6$).

Comparing these steps with the given options, option (0uxx2) correctly identifies all reagents.

$\begin{aligned}$&=$\frac{(2 n) !}{n ! n !}$x^{n} \\

&=$\frac{2^{n}\{n(n-1)(n-2) \ldots 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1\}\{((2 n-1)(2 n-3) \ldots 3 \cdot 1\}}{\{n(n-1)(n-2) \ldots 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1\}^{2}}$x^{n} \\

22043.subject: Mathematics
22043.text: Two finite sets have $m$ and $n$ elements. The total number of proper subsets of the first set is 119 more than the total number of subsets of the second set. Find the value of $m-n$
22043.sol:
The number of subsets of a set with $m$ elements is $2^m$. The number of proper subsets of the first set is $2^m - 1$.

The number of subsets of the second set is $2^n$.

According to the problem, $2^m - 1 = 2^n + 119$.

Rearranging the equation, we get $2^m - 2^n = 120$.

Factoring out $2^n$, we have $2^n(2^{m-n} - 1) = 120$.

Expressing 120 as a product of a power of 2 and an odd number, $120 = 8 \times 15 = 2^3 \times (2^4 - 1)$.

Comparing the two sides, we get $n = 3$ and $m - n = 4$.

Therefore, $m - n = 4$.

Answer: $4$

23308.text: A count rate meter shows a count of $240$ per min from a given radioactive source. One hour later, the meter shows a count rate of $30$ per min. The half-life of the source is

In radioactive decay, the decay rate is proportional to the amount of substance. So, for change of count rate from 240 per min to 30 per min, let $N$ be the number of half-life passed in one hour. Then,
$\frac{240}{2^{N}}=30\Rightarrow \quad 2^{N}=8\Rightarrow \quad N=3$
Half-life, $t_{1 / 2}=\frac{1 h}{3}=\frac{60}{3} \mathrm{ min}=20 \mathrm{ min}$

23724.subject: Physics
23724.text: A bat emitting an ultrasonic wave of frequency $4.5 \times 10^4 \mathrm{ Hz}$ at speed of $6 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ between two parallel walls. The two frequencies heard by the bat will be
23724.sol:
The frequency of the source is $f_0 = 4.5 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz}$. The speed of the bat is $v_b = 6 \text{ m/s}$. The speed of sound in air is taken as $v = 330 \text{ m/s}$.

When the bat moves towards one wall, the wall acts as a stationary observer receiving the sound and then as a stationary source reflecting it back to the moving bat. The frequency $f_1$ heard by the bat from the wall it is moving towards is given by the Doppler effect formula for a moving observer and stationary source: $f_1 = f_0 \left( \dfrac{v + v_b}{v} \right) = 4.5 \times 10^4 \left( \dfrac{330 + 6}{330} \right) = 4.5 \times 10^4 \left( \dfrac{336}{330} \right) \approx 4.58 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz}$.

However, considering the reflection from the wall, the frequency $f_1$ received by the bat is $f_1 = f_0 \left( \dfrac{v + v_b}{v - v_b} \right) = 4.5 \times 10^4 \left( \dfrac{330 + 6}{330 - 6} \right) = 4.5 \times 10^4 \left( \dfrac{336}{324} \right) \approx 4.666 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz} \approx 4.67 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz}$.

Similarly, for the wall the bat is moving away from, the frequency $f_2$ heard by the bat is $f_2 = f_0 \left( \dfrac{v - v_b}{v + v_b} \right) = 4.5 \times 10^4 \left( \dfrac{330 - 6}{330 + 6} \right) = 4.5 \times 10^4 \left( \dfrac{324}{336} \right) \approx 4.339 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz} \approx 4.34 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz}$.

Thus, the two frequencies are $4.67 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz}$ and $4.34 \times 10^4 \text{ Hz}$.

Answer: $4.67 \times 10^4 \mathrm{ Hz}, 4.34 \times 10^4 \mathrm{ Hz}$

25275.subject: Mathematics
25275.text: The area of the region $\left\{\left(x, y\right)$: xy \le 8, 1 \le y \le {x}^{2}\right\}$ is$
25275.sol:
To draw the inequality, let us draw the equation
$xy = 8$ and $y = 1$ and $y = {x}^{2}$
For point of intersection
(i) $xy = 8$ and $y = 1 ⇒ A ( 8,1 )$
(ii) $xy = 8$ and $y = {x}^{2} ⇒ {x}^{3} = 8 ⇒ x = 2 ⇒ B ( 2, 4 )$
(iii) $y = {x}^{2}$ and $y = 1 ⇒ C\left(1, 1\right)$ and $D\left(1, 1\right)$
Now $xy \le 8 ⇒$ region which contains origin
$y \ge 1 ⇒$ region above line $y = 1$
$y \le {x}^{2} ⇒$ region outside the parabola
Now required area
Method I:
Using x-axis:
$A = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{2}\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) ⋅ dx + \mathop{∫}_{2}^{8}\left(\dfrac{8}{x} - 1\right) ⋅ dx$
$A = {\left[\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3} - x\right]}_{1}^{2} + {\left[8lnx - x\right]}_{2}^{8}$
$A = - \dfrac{14}{3} + 16ln2$
Method II:
Using y-axis:
$A = \mathop{∫}_{1}^{4}\left(\dfrac{8}{y} - \sqrt{y}\right) ⋅ dy$
$A = {\left[8lny - \dfrac{2}{3}{y}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right]}_{1}^{4} ⇒ A = - \dfrac{14}{3} + 16ln2$
Note: The question should include bounded area term as in ${2}^{nd}$ quadrant there exist a area which satisfy the inequality and is unbounded.

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(5 + 5\right) = 5$

Hence, Mean deviation about mean will be,

$= \dfrac{3 \times 5 + 2 \times 4 + 1 \times 4 + 2 \times 2 + 4 \times 2 + 5 \times 3}{20}$

$= \dfrac{54}{20} = 2 . 7$

And Mean deviation about median

$= \dfrac{2 \times 5 + 1 \times 4 + 0 + 3 \times 2 + 5 \times 2 + 6 \times 3}{20}$

$= \dfrac{4 . 8}{20} = 2 . 4$

$P \to 3; Q \to 2; R \to 4; S \to 5$

$∴$ Option A is correct.

28791.text:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R .$

Assertion A: The spin only magnetic moment value for ${\left[Fe ( CN{)}_{6}\right]}^{3 -}$ is $1 . 74BM,$ whereas for [Fe(H2O)6]${\left[Fe{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{3 +}$ is $5 . 92BM .$

$[ Fe ( {H}_{2}O{)}_{6}{]}^{3 +}$ has magnetic moment value of $5 . 92BM$ because ${H}_{2}O$ is a weak ligand and pairing will not occur. It involves ${sp}^{3}{d}^{2}$ hybridisation with five unpaired electrons (because magnetic moment is equal to $5 . 92BM$) and outer orbital complex is formed. Magnetic moment can be calculated by the formula ${\mu}_{m} = \sqrt{n ( n + 2 )}$ $BM$ where, ${\mu}_{m} =$magnetic moment, $n =$number of unpaired electron(s).

${\mu}_{m} = 1 . 74BM, n = 1{\mu}_{m} = 5 . 92BM, n = 5$

In $[ Fe ( CN{)}_{6}{]}^{3 –}$complex ${CN}^{-}$ is stronger ligand than ${H}_{2}O$ according to spectrochemical series. Hence, four electrons will pair itself. It involves ${d}^{2}{sp}^{3}$hybridisation with one unpaired electron and inner orbital complex is formed and has a value of only $1 . 74BM$.

In Bothe the complexes the oxidation state of iron is +3.

29552.sol: The addition of phosphates in water enhances algae growth. Such profuse growth of algae, covers the water surface and reduces the oxygen concentration in water. This leads to anaerobic conditions, commonly with accumulation of abnoxious decay and animal death. Thus, bloom-infested water inhibits the growth of other living organisms in the water body. This process in which nutrient enriched water bodies support a dense plant population, which kills animal life by depriving it of oxygen and results in subsequent loss of biodiversity is known as Eutrophication.

33868.text: Let $n$ denote the number of solutions of the equation ${z}^{2} + 3\overset{¯}{z} = 0,$ where $z$ is a complex number. Then the value of $\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{{n}^{k}}$ is equal to
33868.sol:
Given ${z}^{2} + 3\overset{¯}{z} = 0$

Put $z = x + iy,$ then we know that $\overset{¯}{z} = x - iy,$ hence, we have

${\left(x + iy\right)}^{2} + 3\left(x - iy\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {i}^{2}{y}^{2} + 2ixy + 3x - 3iy = 0$

We also, know that ${i}^{2} = - 1,$ hence, we get

$⇒ {x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 2ixy + 3x - 3iy = 0$

$⇒ \left({x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 3x\right) + i ( 2xy - 3y ) = 0 + i0$

On comparing the real and imaginary parts, we get

${x}^{2} - {y}^{2} + 3x = 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

And $2xy - 3y = 0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$⇒ y\left(2x - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{3}{2}, y = 0$

Put $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$ in equation $\left(1\right),$ we get $\dfrac{9}{4} - {y}^{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} = 0$

$⇒ {y}^{2} = \dfrac{27}{4}$

$⇒ y = \pm \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} .$

$⇒ \left(x, y\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right), \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{- 3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) .$

Now, put $y = 0,$ in the equation $\left(1\right),$ we get ${x}^{2} + 3x = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, - 3 .$

$∴ \left(x, y\right) = \left(0, 0\right), \left(- 3, 0\right) .$

$∴$ No of solutions$= n = 4$

Now, $\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{\infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{{n}^{k}}\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{\infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{{4}^{k}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{1} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{16} + \dfrac{1}{64} + \ldots \ldots$

The above progression is a geometric progression, with first term $a = 1$ and common ratio $r = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and the sum of infinite terms of the geometric progression is $\dfrac{a}{1 - r}$

Thus, $\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{\infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{{n}^{k}}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)} = \dfrac{4}{3} .$

34763.text: Let $S = \left(0, 2\pi\right) - \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right\}$. Let $y = y\left(x\right)$, $x \in S$, be the solution curve of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + sin2x}, y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$. If the sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection of the curve $y = y\left(x\right)$ with the curve $y = \sqrt{2}sinx$ is $\dfrac{k\pi}{12}$, then $k$ is equal to _____.
34763.sol:
Given differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + sin2x}$

$∫ dy = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{{\left(sinx + cosx\right)}^{2}}$

$∫ dy = ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{{\left(1 + tanx\right)}^{2}}$

$y = - \dfrac{1}{1 + tanx} + C$

So $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

So $\dfrac{1}{2} = - \dfrac{1}{2} + C$$⇒ C = 1$

So $y = \dfrac{- 1}{1 + tanx} + 1$

$y = \dfrac{- 1 + 1 + tanx}{1 + tanx}$

$y = \dfrac{tanx}{1 + tanx}$

Solving this equation with $y = \sqrt{2}sinx$

$\dfrac{tanx}{1 + tanx} = \sqrt{2}sinx$

i.e. $sinx = 0, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = sinx + cosx$

$x = \pi$

or $\dfrac{1}{2} = sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$⇒ sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

$x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6}, 2\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}, x = \dfrac{13\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$x = \dfrac{7\pi}{12}, x = \dfrac{23\pi}{12}$

Hence sum of abscissas of all the points of intersection

$= \pi + \dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{23\pi}{12}$

$= \dfrac{12\pi + 7\pi + 23}{12} = \dfrac{42\pi}{12}$

$\dfrac{k\pi}{12} = \dfrac{42\pi}{12} ⇒ k = 42$

37577.text:
Consider the following frequency distribution:

Class: $0 - 6$ $6 - 12$ $12 - 18$ $18 - 24$ $24 - 30$
Frequency: $a$ $b$ $12$ $9$ $5$

If mean $= \dfrac{309}{22}$ and median $= 14,$ then the value $( a - b{)}^{2}$ is equal to
37577.sol:
Class Frequency Mid-point $\left({x}_{i}\right)$ ${f}_{i}{x}_{i}$
$0 - 6$ $a$ $\dfrac{0 + 6}{2} = 3$ $3a$
$6 - 12$ $b$ $\dfrac{6 + 12}{2} = 9$ $9b$
$12 - 18$ $12$ $\dfrac{12 + 18}{2} = 15$ $180$
$18 - 24$ $9$ $\dfrac{18 + 24}{2} = 21$ $189$
$24 - 30$ $5$ $\dfrac{24 + 30}{2} = 27$ $135$
$N = \left(26 + a + b\right)$ $\left(504 + 3a + 9b\right)$

We know that, mean$= \dfrac{∑ {f}_{i}{x}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}}$

Given, mean$= \dfrac{309}{22}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3a + 9b + 180 + 189 + 135}{a + b + 26} = \dfrac{309}{22}$

$⇒ \dfrac{504 + 3a + 9b}{a + b + 26} = \dfrac{309}{22}$

$⇒ 66a + 198b + 11088 = 309a + 309b + 8034$

$⇒ 243a + 111b = 3054$

$⇒ 81a + 37b = 1018 . . . \left(1\right)$

Now, median$= 14,$ which lies in the interval $12 - 18,$ thus $12 - 18$ is the median class and we have $= l + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{N}{2} - c\right) \times h}{f},$

Where, $l$ is the lower limit of the median class i.e. $l = 12, c$ is the cumulative frequency of the class above the median class i.e. $c = a + b, f$ is the frequency of the median class i.e. $f = 12$ and $h$ is the length of the interval i.e. $h = 6 .$

Thus, we have $12 + \left(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a + b + 26}{2}\right) - ( a + b )}{12}\right) \times 6 = 14$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a + b + 26 - 2a - 2b}{2}\right)}{2} = 14 - 12$

$⇒ \dfrac{26 - a - b}{4} = 2$

$⇒ 26 - a - b = 8$

$⇒ a + b = 18 . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving the equations $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right),$ we get $a = 8, b = 10 .$

$∴ {\left(a - b\right)}^{2} = {\left(8 - 10\right)}^{2} = 4 .$

${\left(81\right)}^{\sin^{2}x} = t$

$t + \dfrac{81}{t} = 30$

${t}^{2} - 30t + 81 = 0$

$\left(t - 3\right)\left(t - 27\right) = 0$

${\left(81\right)}^{\sin^{2}x} = {3}^{1}$ or ${\left(81\right)}^{\sin^{2}x} = {3}^{3}$

${3}^{4\sin^{2}x} = {3}^{1}$ or ${3}^{4\sin^{2}x} = {3}^{3}$

$\sin^{2}x = \dfrac{1}{4}$ or $\sin^{2}x = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Hence, total $4$ solution.

$a = \dfrac{\left({m}_{2} - {m}_{1}\right)}{\left({m}_{2} + {m}_{1}\right)}g$

Since $a = \dfrac{g}{2}$

$\dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{\left({m}_{2} - {m}_{1}\right)}{\left({m}_{2} + {m}_{1}\right)}g ⇒ \dfrac{g}{2} = \dfrac{\left(L - l\right) - l}{L}g ⇒ l = \dfrac{L}{4} = \dfrac{L}{x}$

$⇒ x = 4$

42504.subject: Physics
42504.text: For a nucleus of mass number $A$ and radius $R$, the mass density of nucleus can be represented as
42504.sol:
The mass density ( $\rho$) of a nucleus is defined as the ratio of its mass to its volume:
$\rho=$ Mass of nucleus / Volume of nucleus
For a spherical nucleus with radius R , the volume is:
$\text{ Volume }=(4 / 3) \pi R^3$
The mass of the nucleus is related to the mass number A :
$\text{ Mass }-\mathrm{A} \times \mathrm{m} \text{ _u }$
(where m_u is the atomic mass unit, approximately $1.66 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}$)
Therefore:
$\rho=\left(\mathrm{A} \times \mathrm{m} \_\mathrm{u}\right) /\left[(4 / 3) \pi \mathrm{R}^3\right]$
Now, there's an important relationship between the mass number A and nuclear radius R. Empirically, it has been found that:
$\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{Ro} * \mathrm{~A}^{\wedge}(1 / 3)$
Where Ro is a constant approximately equal to $1.2 \times 10^{-15} \mathrm{~m}(1.2$ fermi).
Substituting this into the density equation:
$\begin{aligned}
& \rho=\left(\mathrm{A} \times \mathrm{m} \_\mathrm{u}\right) /\left[(4 / 3) \pi\left(\mathrm{Ro} \times \mathrm{A}^{\wedge}(1 / 3)\right)^3\right] \\ & \rho=(\mathrm{A} \times \mathrm{m} \text{ _u }) /\left[(4 / 3) \pi \mathrm{Ro}^3 \times \mathrm{A}\right] \\ & \rho=\mathrm{m} \_\mathrm{u} /\left[(4 / 3) \pi \mathrm{Ro}^3\right]
\end{aligned}$
This shows that the nuclear density is approximately constant for all nuclei, regardless of their mass number. This is a fundamental property of nuclear matter known as nuclear saturation density.
The numerical value is:
$\rho=2.3 \times 10^{17} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$

43488.text:
If each diode has a forward bias resistance of $25Ω$ in the below circuit,

Which of the following options is correct?
43488.sol:
As the diode ${D}_{2}$ is connected in reverse order, there is no current through it.

The effective resistances of the circuit can, then, be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{R}_{eff} & = & 25 + \dfrac{{\left(25 + 125\right)}^{2}}{\left(25 + 125\right) + \left(25 + 125\right)}Ω \\ & = & 100Ω\end{cases}$

Each current through the diodes can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}{I}_{1} & = & \left(\dfrac{5V}{100Ω}\right) \\ & = & 0 . 05A\end{cases}$

As the diode ${D}_{2}$ is non-conducting, the current ${I}_{1}$ will be divided equally among the other two diodes ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{3}$.

Hence, the currents in the diodes can be written as

$\begin{cases}{I}_{2} & = & \dfrac{0 . 05A}{2} \\ & = & 0 . 025A \\ {I}_{4} & = & 0 . 025A\end{cases}$

Thus,

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{I}_{1}}{{I}_{2}} & = & \dfrac{0 . 05A}{0 . 025A} \\ & = & 2\end{cases}$

43998.subject: Physics
43998.text:
Consider an ideal gas confined in an isolated closed chamber. As the gas undergoes an adiabatic expansion, the average time of collision between molecules increases as ${V}^{q}$ , where $V$ is the volume of the gas. The value of $q$ is:

$\left(\gamma = \dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{v}}\right)$
43998.sol:
For an adiabatic process $T{V}^{\gamma - 1} =$ constant.
We know that average time of collision between molecules

$τ = \dfrac{1}{n\pi\sqrt{2}{v}_{rms}{d}^{2}}$

where, $n =$ number of molecules per unit volume ${V}_{rms} =$ rms velocity of molecules

As $n ∝ \dfrac{1}{V}$ and ${v}_{rms} ∝ \sqrt{T}$

$τ ∝ \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{T}}$

Thus, we can write

$n = {K}_{1}{V}^{- 1}$ and ${V}_{rms} = {K}_{2}T\dfrac{1}{2}$.

where, ${K}_{1}$ and ${K}_{2}$ are constants.

For adiabatic process, $T{V}^{\gamma - 1} =$ constant. Thus, we can write

$τ ∝ V{T}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} ∝ V\left({V}^{1 - \gamma}\right)\dfrac{- 1}{2}$

or $τ ∝ V\dfrac{\gamma + 1}{2}$

45009.subject: Botany
45009.text: Nitrogen-fixation in root nodules of  Alnus is brought about by
45009.sol:
Nitrogen is the most critical element. Atmosphere is the greatest reservior of nitrogen. Molecular nitrogen cannot be utilized directly by plants. It has to be fixed or converted into compounds prior to utilization. Symbiotic nitrogen fixation is accomplished by Rhizobium species, which occurs on the roots of leguminous plants. Certain non-leguminous plants also form nodules to fix nitrogen. The best known example in temperate region is alder (Alnus sp.) The bacteria involved in nodule formation is an Actinomycetes, the Frankia.
 Clostridium is anaerobic, saprotrophic, free-living nitrogen fixing bacteria. Bradyrhizobium is symbiont in plants of Parasponia and soyabean.
The  Azorhizobium forms both stem and root nodules in Sesbania (aquatic plant).

46793.sol:
DNA ase (or deoxyribonuclease) or simply nuclease is an enzyme which breaks down DNA by hydrolysis of the phosphodiester bonds of its sugar-phosphate back-bone. Depending on the position of hydrolysing phosphodiester bonds, nucleases are of two types:
(i) Endonucleases (ii)Exonucleases.
Endonucleases hydrolyse internal phosphodiester bonds in a polynucleotide chain (i.e., DNA). While exonucleases hydrolyse terminal phosphodiester bonds in a polynucleotide chain (i.e., DNA).

(i) w.r.t. $t$, we get $\quad 2 A A^{\prime}=37(2 t)$ After $t=1 \mathrm{ h}$, we get $2 \sqrt{37} A^{\prime}=2(37)$ After $t=1 \mathrm{ h}$, we get $\Rightarrow \quad A^{\prime}=\sqrt{37}$ Thus, rate at which shortest distance $A$ changes with time is $\sqrt{37} \mathrm{ km} / \mathrm{h}$.

55284.text: What is the number of moles of hydrogen atoms required to reduce one mole of nitroethane completely using Sn and HCl ?
55284.sol:
Reduction of nitroethane to ethylamine requires hydrogen atoms as reducing agents. The balanced equation illustrates the stoichiometry:

$\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 NO_2 + 6[H] \rightarrow CH_3 CH_2 NH_2 + 2H_2 O}$

The coefficient confirms 6 moles of hydrogen atoms are needed per mole of nitroethane.

An oxidation state analysis supports this. In $\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 NO_2}$, nitrogen is +5, while in $\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 NH_2 }$, it is −1. The 6-electron reduction corresponds to 6 atoms of hydrogen.

Therefore, the required number is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

55441.text: Which of the following is found to raise the HDL level in the blood?
55441.sol:
Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated fatty acids that are known to increase the level of High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL), which is considered good cholesterol, in the blood. They also help in lowering triglyceride levels, thereby reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

Trans fats, on the other hand, lower HDL levels and raise LDL (bad cholesterol) levels.

Answer: Omega-3 fatty acids

56814.subject: Chemistry
56814.text: What is the change in oxidation number of Pb at positive electrode of lead accumulator acting as galvanic cell ?
56814.sol:
In a lead accumulator acting as a galvanic cell (discharging), the positive electrode acts as the cathode where reduction takes place.

The reaction at the positive electrode is:
$PbO_2(s) + SO_4^{2-}(aq) + 4H^+(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow PbSO_4(s) + 2H_2O(l)$

The oxidation state of Pb in $PbO_2$ is $+4$.
The oxidation state of Pb in $PbSO_4$ is $+2$.

The oxidation number of Pb changes from $+4$ to $+2$, which means it decreases by $2$.

Answer: decreases by 2

57961.subject: Chemistry
57961.text: Which of the following aqueous salt solutions has the least pH value ?
57961.sol:
$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a weak acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$), so its aqueous solution is basic with $\text{pH} > 7$.

$\text{CuCl}_2$ is a salt of a weak base ($\text{Cu(OH)}_2$) and a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$), so its aqueous solution undergoes cationic hydrolysis to give an acidic solution with $\text{pH} < 7$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a weak acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$), so its aqueous solution is basic with $\text{pH} > 7$.

$\text{NaNO}_3$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a strong acid ($\text{HNO}_3$), so its aqueous solution is neutral with $\text{pH} = 7$.

Therefore, $\text{CuCl}_2$ has the least pH value.

Answer: $\text{CuCl}_2$

60572.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y = 2^{kx}$ and $x = 0, x = 2$, in first quadrant is $\dfrac{2}{\log 2}$, then the value of $k$ is
60572.sol:
The area of the region is given by

$A = \int_{0}^{2} 2^{kx} dx$

$A = \left[ \dfrac{2^{kx}}{k \log 2} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$A = \dfrac{2^{2k} - 1}{k \log 2}$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{2}{\log 2}$:

$\dfrac{2^{2k} - 1}{k \log 2} = \dfrac{2}{\log 2}$

$2^{2k} - 1 = 2k$

Checking the given options, for $k = \dfrac{1}{2}$:

$2^{2(1/2)} - 1 = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$2 - 1 = 1$

This satisfies the equation, hence $k = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

61263.text: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =\cos(x + y)$ is...
61263.sol:
Let $x + y = v$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1$

Substituting this in the given differential equation:

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1 = \cos v$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + \cos v$

$\dfrac{dv}{1 + \cos v} = dx$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{dv}{2 \cos^2\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)} = \int dx$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \int \sec^2\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right) dv = \int dx$

$\tan\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right) = x + c$

Substituting $v = x + y$:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = x + c$

61629.sol:
Let $x = \cos \theta$.

Substituting this in the given expression:

$\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{1 + x}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos \theta}{1 + \cos \theta}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \sin^2(\theta/2)}{2 \cos^2(\theta/2)}} = \tan \left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)

The expression for $y$ becomes:

$y = \cos^2 $\left[\cot^{-1} \left(\tan \left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)\right]

Using$ the identity\tan$\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \cot \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right):

$y = \cos^2 $\left[\cot^{-1}\left(\cot \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right)\right]

$y = \cos^2 $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)

$y = \sin^2 $\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$

Using the half-angle formula $\sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1 - \cos \theta}{2}$:

$y = \dfrac{1 - x}{2}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-1}{2}$

Evaluating $f(f(x))$:

62209.subject: Mathematics
62209.text: If $\int \frac{\left(x^4+1\right)}{x\left(x^2+1\right)^2} \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{A} \log |x|+\frac{\mathrm{B}}{1+x^2}+\mathrm{c}$, then $\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}$ is (where c is the constant of integration)
62209.sol:
Let $I = \int \frac{x^4+1}{x(x^2+1)^2} \, dx$.

Rewriting the numerator as $x^4+1 = (x^2+1)^2 - 2x^2$ allows the integrand to be expressed as:

$\frac{(x^2+1)^2 - 2x^2}{x(x^2+1)^2} = \frac{1}{x} - \frac{2x}{(x^2+1)^2}$.

Integrating term by term yields:

$I = \int \frac{1}{x} \, dx - \int \frac{2x}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx = \log |x| - \int \frac{2x}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx$.

Using the substitution $u = x^2+1$ where $du = 2x \, dx$, the second term becomes:

$\int \frac{1}{u^2} \, du = -\frac{1}{u} + C = -\frac{1}{x^2+1} + C$.

Thus, the integral is:

$I = \log |x| + \frac{1}{x^2+1} + c$.

Comparing with the form $A \log |x| + \frac{B}{1+x^2} + c$, we identify $A = 1$ and $B = 1$.

Therefore, $A - B = 0$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{0}$

63163.text: If the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is expressed as the sum of a symmetric matrix B and a skew symmetric matrix C then which of the following relations is correct?
63163.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

The transpose of matrix $A$ is $A^T = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

Any square matrix can be expressed as the sum of a symmetric matrix $B$ and a skew-symmetric matrix $C$, where $B = \dfrac{1}{2}(A + A^T)$ and $C = \dfrac{1}{2}(A - A^T)$

$B = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \right) = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \right) = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

Calculating the determinants of $A$, $B$, and $C$:

$|A| = (4)(2) - (1)(3) = 5$

$|B| = (4)(2) - (2)(2) = 4$

$|C| = (0)(0) - (-1)(1) = 1$

Checking the given relations, we find that $|B| + |C| = 4 + 1 = 5$

Therefore, $|A| = |B| + |C|$

Answer: $|A| = |B| + |C|$

65109.text: A unit vector coplanar with $\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and perpendicular to $\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is
65109.sol:
Let the required vector be $\vec{v} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$.

Since $\vec{v}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, it must be perpendicular to their cross product $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$.

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 2 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} = -3\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$

Thus, $\vec{v} \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = 0 \Rightarrow -3x + y + z = 0$

Also, $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, so $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$.

$x + y + z = 0$

Subtracting the two equations gives $-4x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0$.

Substituting $x = 0$ into $x + y + z = 0$ gives $y = -z$.

So the vector is of the form $\vec{v} = y\hat{j} - y\hat{k} = y(\hat{j} - \hat{k})$.

Since $\vec{v}$ is a unit vector, $|\vec{v}| = 1$.

$\sqrt{y^2 + (-y)^2} = 1 \Rightarrow \sqrt{2y^2} = 1 \Rightarrow y = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Therefore, the required unit vector is $\pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{j} - \hat{k})$.

Answer: $\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{j} - \hat{k})$

66586.text: An electron accelerated by a potential difference 'V' has de-Broglie wavelength ' $\lambda$ '. If the electron is accelerated by a potential difference ' 9 V ', its de-Broglie wavelength will be
66586.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of an electron accelerated through a potential difference $V$ is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}$ where $h$ is Planck’s constant, $m$ is the electron mass, and $e$ is the electron charge.

This implies $\lambda$ is inversely proportional to $\sqrt{V}, so \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$ and thus $\lambda = \frac{C}{\sqrt{V}}$ where $C = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2me}}$.

For a potential difference of $9V$, the corresponding wavelength $\lambda'$ satisfies $\lambda' = \frac{C}{\sqrt{9V}} = \frac{C}{3\sqrt{V}} = \frac{\lambda}{3}$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\frac{\lambda}{3}}$

66808.subject: Physics
66808.text: A conducting ring of certain resistance is falling towards a current carrying straight long conductor. The ring and conductor are in the same plane. Then
options: induced current in the coil is zero.
induced current in the coil is anticlockwise.
induced current in the coil is clockwise.
66808.sol:
The induced current direction is determined by applying Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law.

The magnetic field above a rightward-carrying conductor points out of the page, as given by the right-hand thumb rule. As the ring falls toward the conductor, the magnetic field strength $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$ increases since distance $r$ decreases. This results in an increasing magnetic flux directed out of the page through the ring.

Lenz's Law requires that the induced current opposes this flux increase. The induced current must therefore produce a magnetic field directed into the page. Applying the right-hand curl rule shows that this corresponds to a clockwise current in the ring.

The induced current flows clockwise.

67020.subject: Physics
67020.text: Following figure indicates the electric potential V as a function through 4 regions on x-axis. Which of the following is correct for the electric field E in these regions?
67020.sol:
The relation between electric field $E$ and electric potential $V$ is given by $E = -\dfrac{dV}{dx}$.

The magnitude of the electric field is equal to the magnitude of the slope of the $V-x$ graph.

In regions 1 and 3, the potential $V$ is constant. Therefore, the slope is zero, which means $E_1 = 0$ and $E_3 = 0$. Thus, $E_1 = E_3$.

In region 2, the magnitude of the electric field is $E_2 = \left| \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta x} \right| = \dfrac{V_C - V_B}{x_C - x_B}$.

In region 4, the magnitude of the electric field is $E_4 = \left| \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta x} \right| = \dfrac{V_D - V_E}{x_E - x_D} = \dfrac{V_C - 0}{x_E - x_D}$.

From the given graph, the horizontal widths of regions 2 and 4 are equal, i.e., $x_C - x_B = x_E - x_D$.

Since $V_B > 0$, the change in potential in region 4 ($V_C$) is greater than the change in potential in region 2 ($V_C - V_B$).

Therefore, the slope in region 4 is steeper than in region 2, which implies $E_4 > E_2$.

Combining these observations, we get $E_1 = E_3$ and $E_2 < E_4$.

Answer: $E_1 = E_3$ and $E_2 < E_4$

68036.text: Error in the measurement of radius of the sphere is $2 \%$. The error in the calculated value of its volume is
68036.sol:
The volume of a sphere is given by $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, where $r$ is the radius.

Since $V$ is proportional to $r^3$, the percentage error in volume relates to the percentage error in radius by the power rule:
$\frac{\Delta V}{V} \times 100\% = 3 \left( \frac{\Delta r}{r} \times100\% \right)$

Given that the radius has a $2\%$ error, the volume error becomes:
$\frac{\Delta V}{V} \times100\% = 3 \times2\% = 6\%$

Answer: $\$boxed{$\text{C}$$}$

69469.text: In the logic circuit given, $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C are the inputs and Y is the output. The output Y is HIGH
69469.sol:
Output Y is HIGH only when A=1, B=0, C=0.

The circuit consists of a NOR gate with inputs B and C, followed by an AND gate with inputs A and the NOR output. The Boolean expression is $Y = A \cdot \overline{B+C}$.

Evaluating for each case:

When A=1, B=1, C=1: $Y = 1 \cdot \overline{1+1} = 1 \cdot 0 = 0$
When A=0, B=0, C=0: $Y = 0 \cdot \overline{0+0} = 0 \cdot 1 = 0$
When A=1, B=0, C=0: $Y = 1 \cdot \overline{0+0} = 1 \cdot 1 = 1$
When A=1, B=0, C=1: $Y = 1 \cdot \overline{0+1} = 1 \cdot 0 = 0$

70455.text: Waves having a velocity 10m/s, strike a stationary boat near the sea shore. The distance between two consecutive crests of the waves is 40m. After how many second, the consecutive waves strike the boat?
70455.sol:
Given velocity of waves, $v = 10$ m/s.

Distance between two consecutive crests is the wavelength, $\lambda = 40$ m.

The time interval between consecutive waves striking the stationary boat is the time period $T$.

Using the relation $v = \dfrac{\lambda}{T}$, we get:

$T = \dfrac{\lambda}{v}$

$T = \dfrac{40}{10} = 4$ s.

Answer: $4$ s

71094.subject: Biology
71094.text: The natural selection in which more number of individuals acquire peripheral character value at both ends of the distribution curve is called ----------------- selection.
71094.sol:
Natural selection can be of three main types based on its effect on the distribution of traits in a population:

Stabilizing selection: More individuals acquire the mean character value, and variation is reduced.

Directional selection: More individuals acquire a value other than the mean character value, shifting the peak in one direction.

Disruptive selection: More individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve, leading to a bimodal distribution where extreme traits are favored over intermediate ones.

Therefore, the selection described in the question is disruptive selection.

Answer: disruptive

71294.subject: Biology
71294.text:
Match List I with List II
List I
(Enzymes involved in DNA replication)		List II
(Function.)
(A) Helicase(I) Forms double helix to form daughter DNA molecules.
(B) DNA polymerase(II) Activation of nucleotides.
(C) DNA gyrase(III) Unwinding of DNA.
(D) Phosphorylase(IV) Removal of RNA primers.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
71294.sol:
Helicase is responsible for the unwinding of the DNA double helix by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the complementary nitrogenous bases.

DNA polymerase (specifically DNA polymerase I) has $5' \rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease activity, which is responsible for the removal of RNA primers during DNA replication.

DNA gyrase (a type of topoisomerase) relieves the torsional strain generated during unwinding and introduces negative supercoils, which helps in forming the double helix of daughter DNA molecules.

Phosphorylase is involved in the activation of nucleotides by adding phosphate groups to nucleoside monophosphates to form nucleoside triphosphates.

Thus, the correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (I), (D) - (II)

71507.subject: Biology
71507.text:
Given below are two statements about endosperms in angiosperms.
Statement (I): Coconut has a nuclear type of endosperm with a multicellular outer part and a free nuclear vacuolated center.
Statement (II): In the helobial type of endosperm, the micropylar cell shows free nuclear division whereas the chalazal cell shows wall formation after free nuclear divisions.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71507.sol:
Statement (I) is correct. In coconut, the endosperm is of the nuclear type. The primary endosperm nucleus undergoes successive free nuclear divisions. The outer peripheral part undergoes cellularization to form the multicellular solid endosperm (coconut meat), while the center remains a large vacuole filled with free nuclear endosperm (coconut water).

Statement (II) is incorrect. In the helobial type of endosperm, the first division of the primary endosperm nucleus is followed by the formation of a transverse wall, resulting in a large micropylar chamber and a small chalazal chamber. Subsequent divisions in the micropylar chamber are free nuclear, which are later followed by wall formation (cellularization). The chalazal chamber usually remains undivided or undergoes only a few free nuclear divisions without wall formation.

Therefore, Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

71884.subject: Chemistry
71884.text: What is the pH of buffer solution containing $10$ times higher molar concentration of weak base than the molar concentration of salt of weak base with strong acid at $298$ K? (K_b$ of weak base $= 10^{-5}$)$
71884.sol:
Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a basic buffer:

$pOH = pK_b + \log \left( \dfrac{[Salt]}{[Base]} \right)

Given $ K_b = 10^{-5}$, we have $pK_b = -$\log$(10^{-5}) = 5$.

It is given that the concentration of the weak base is 10$ times the concentration of the salt, so $[Base] = 10 [Salt]$, which gives $\dfrac{[Salt]}{[Base]} = \dfrac{1}{10}$.

Substituting these values into the equation:

$ pOH = 5 + \log \left( \dfrac{1}{10} \right)$

$pOH = 5 - 1 = 4$

At $298$ K, the relationship between pH and pOH is:

$pH + pOH = 14$

$pH = 14 - 4 = 10$

Answer: $10$

72227.subject: Physics
72227.text: A particle of mass '$M$' and charge '$q$' initially at rest is accelerated by a uniform electric field '$E$' through a distance '$D$' and is then allowed to approach a fixed static charge '$Q$' of the same sign. The distance of the closest approach of the charge $q$ is $[\,\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space $]$
72227.sol:
Work done by the uniform electric field on the particle is given by $W = qED$.

By the work-energy theorem, the kinetic energy gained by the particle is $K = qED$.

When the particle approaches the fixed static charge $Q$, its kinetic energy is converted into electrostatic potential energy.

At the distance of closest approach $r$, the velocity of the particle becomes zero and the entire kinetic energy is stored as potential energy.

The electrostatic potential energy at distance $r$ is $U = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{qQ}{r}$.

Equating the kinetic energy and potential energy:

$qED = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{qQ}{r}$

$r = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 ED}$

Answer: $Q/4\pi\epsilon_0 ED$

77426.subject: Mathematics
77426.text: A man at $M$, standing 100 m away from the base (P$) of a chimney of height 50 m, observes the angle of elevation of the highest point (Q$) of the smoke to be $45°$. The highest point of the chimney is at $R$. Further $P$, $R$ and $Q$ are in a straight line and the straight line is perpendicular to $PM$. What is the angle $RMQ$ equal to?
77426.sol:
Let $PM$ be the distance of the man from the base of the chimney, so $PM = 100$ m.

Let $PR$ be the height of the chimney, so $PR = 50$ m.

Let $Q$ be the highest point of the smoke. The angle of elevation of $Q$ from $M$ is $\angle PMQ = 45^{}^{\circ}$.

In $\triangle PMQ$, $\tan(\angle PMQ) = \dfrac{PQ}{PM}$

$\tan(45^{}^{\circ}) = \dfrac{PQ}{100} \Rightarrow PQ = 100$ m.

In $\triangle PMR$, $\tan(\angle PMR) = \dfrac{PR}{PM} = \dfrac{50}{100} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The required angle is $\angle RMQ = \angle PMQ - \angle PMR = 45^{}^{\circ} - \angle PMR$.

Taking tangent on both sides:

$\tan(\angle RMQ) = \tan(45^{}^{\circ} - \angle PMR) = \dfrac{\tan(45^{}^{\circ}) - \tan(\angle PMR)}{1 + \tan(45^{}^{\circ})\tan(\angle PMR)}$

$\tan(\angle RMQ) = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$\angle RMQ = \tan^{-1} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)

Answer: $\tan^{-1} $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

81065.text:
If $60 \%$, of a first order reaction was completed in 60 minutes, $50 \%$ of the same reaction would be completed in approximately:

($\log 4=0$.60, $\log 5=0$.69)
81065.sol:
For a first order reaction
$k=\frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{a}{a-x}$
When t=60 and $x=60 \% \begin{aligned}
k & =\frac{2.303}{60} \log \frac{100}{100-60} \\
& =\frac{2.303}{60} \log \frac{100}{40} \\
& =0.0153
\end{aligned}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
t^{1 / 2} & =\frac{2.303}{0.0153} \log \frac{100}{100-50} \\
& =\frac{2.303}{0.0153} \times \log 2 \\
& =\frac{2.303}{0.0153} \times 0.3010 \\
& =45.31 \mathrm{~min}
\end{aligned}$

84565.subject: Zoology
84565.text: To which type of barriers under innate immunity, do the saliva in the mouth and the tears from the eyes, belong?
84565.sol:
Innate immunity is the resistance to infection, which an individual possesses by virtue of his/her genetic and constitutional make up. Thus, it comprises all those defence elements with which an individual is born and, which are always available to protect a living body. Physiological barriers like body temperature, $\mathrm{pH}$ of the body fluid, and various body secretions (saliva, tears) prevent growth of many disease causing micro-organisms.
Skin is the physical barrier of the body. Its outer tough layer the stratum corneum prevents the entry of bacteria and viruses.

85452.subject: Zoology
85452.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
options: Inbreeding is essential to evolve purelines in any animal.
Inbreeding helps in accumulation of superior genes and elimination of undesirable genes.
Inbreeding selects harmful recessive genes that reduce fertility and productivity.
85452.sol:
The breeding strategy based on inbreeding is as follows. Superior cows and the superior bulls of the same breed are identified and mated in pairs. The progeny obtained from such mating is evaluated and superior males and females are identified for further mating. A superior female, in the case of cattle, is the cow that produces more milk or lactation. On the other hand, a superior male is that bull, which gives rise to superior progeny as compared to those of other males. Inbreeding, as a rule, increases homozygosity.

  • Advantage: Inbreeding exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection. It also helps in the accumulation of superior genes and elimination of less desirable genes. Therefore, this approach increases the productivity of inbred population.
  • Disadvantage: But continued inbreeding, especially close inbreeding, usually reduces fertility and even productivity (inbreeding depression). Whenever this becomes a problem the selected animals of the breeding population should be mated with such superior animals of the same breed that are unrelated to those in the breeding population.

Halogenation of ketones is an interesting reaction. For example, it is involved in the preparation of haloforms. Halogenation using molecular halogen takes place at the $\alpha$ position to the carbonyl group in the presence of an acid or a base. In a basic medium, the stability of carbanion is important. In an acidic medium stability of enol form is important, as the reaction goes through enol.


An $\alpha$-halogenated ketone undergoes subsequent halogenation to form polyhalogenated ketone. Chloroform is prepared by the action of sodium hypochlorite on acetone. In this process trichloroacetone is formed as an intermediate. Trichloroacetone can react with hydroxide ion in two possible ways as shown below.
(i) $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{COCH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HO}^{-}} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{CHCl}_3$
(ii) $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{COCH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HO}^{-}} \mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{CH}_4$

In an alkaline medium, reaction (i) is favoured over reaction (ii) due to stabilization of carbanion.

90002.text: Number of integral terms in the expansion of ${\left(\sqrt{5} + 78\right)}^{1024}$ is
90002.sol:
We have, ${T}_{r = 1}{=}^{1024}{C}_{r}\left(5\right)\dfrac{\left(1024 - r\right)}{2}\left(7\right)\dfrac{r}{8}$
This is an integer, if $1024 - r$ is an even number and $r$ is a multiple of $8$

i.e. when $r$ is a multiple of $8$ since $0 \le r \le 1024$

The number of multiples of $8$ which lies between $0$ and $1024$ is
$1024 = 0 + \left(n - 1\right)8$
$⇒ n - 1 = \dfrac{1024}{8} = 128$
$⇒ n = 129$

90068.sol:
Let the equation of the circle is ${\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 3\right)}^{2} + \lambda\left(x + y - 4\right) = 0$
$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + \left(\lambda - 2\right)x + \left(\lambda - 6\right)y + \left(10 - 4\lambda\right) = 0$
which is orthogonal to $x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$
Now, ${2g}_{1}{g}_{2} + 2{f}_{1}{f}_{2} = {c}_{1} + {c}_{2}$ implies $0 + 0 = 10 - 4\lambda - 4 ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3}{2}$
Hence, the equation of the circle is
$x^{2} + y^{2} - \dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{9y}{2} + 4 = 0$
$Radius = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{16} + \dfrac{81}{16} - 4} = \sqrt{\dfrac{18}{16}}$
$= \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}$

90895.text: An aeroplane flying horizontally $1$ km above the ground is observed at an elevation of ${60}^{o}$ and after $10$ seconds the elevation is observed to be ${30}^{o}$. The uniform speed of the aeroplane (in $km / h$), is
90895.sol:
Let, $d$ is the distance covered by aeroplane in $10$ sec.

Let, the height at which the plane is flying be $H = 1km$

$⇒ H = AC = BD = 1km$

In $∆ OAC$,
$tan ⁡ {60}^{o} = \dfrac{AC}{OC}$

$OC = 1cot ⁡ {60}^{o}$...(i)

In $∆ OBD$,
$tan ⁡ {30}^{o} = \dfrac{BD}{OD}$

$OD = 1cot ⁡ {30}^{o}$...(ii)
Now,
$d = AB = CD = OD - OC$
$d = cot ⁡ {30}^{o} - cot ⁡ {60}^{o}$

$Speed = \dfrac{d}{t} = \dfrac{cot ⁡ {30}^{o} - cot ⁡ {60}^{o}}{10}km / sec$

Speed in $km / h$

$= \dfrac{cot ⁡ {30}^{o} - cot ⁡ {60}^{o}}{10} \times 60 \times 60$

$= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{10} \times 3600$

$= 240\sqrt{3}km / h$

91670.text: The probability of a problem being solved by $3$ students independently are $\dfrac{1}{2}$, $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $\alpha$ respectively. If the probability that the problem is solved is $P   \left(S\right), then $P   $\left(S\right)$lies in $the interval (where, \alpha \in \left(0, 1\right))$
91670.sol:
Let $3$ students are $A, B, C$ and their probability of solving problems is $P \left(A\right), P \left(B\right), P \left(C\right)$ respectively.
$P\left(A\right) = \dfrac{1}{2},$ P$\left(B\right) =\dfrac{1}{3},$ P$\left(C\right) =\alpha$
Probability of the problem is being solved,
$P\left(S\right) =1 - P ( A^{C} \cap B^{C} \cap C^{C} )$
$= 1 - P \left(A^{C}\right)$ P $\left(B^{C}\right)$ P ( C^{C} )$
$= 1 - $\left(1 - P\left(A\right)\right)\left(1 - P \left(B\right)\right)\left(1 - P \left(C\right)\right)$
$= 1 - \$left($\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\left(1 - \alpha\right)
$= $\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3}\alpha$

Hence, $P \left(S\right)$ \in \$ left(\dfrac{2}{3},1\right)$

96216.text: Colchicine is a chemical that stops chromatids from separating during mitosis. If a cell is treated with colchicine, at which stage of mitosis will this cell reach but not complete?
96216.sol: Colchicine is a mitotic inhibitor. It does not allow spindle fibres to be formed. Thus, condensation of chromosomes will occur and prophase will be completed. But metaphase won't be completed. The metaphase stage is characterized by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.

96484.text: According to Robert Constanza, what percentage of the total cost of various ecosystem services is used for nutrient recycling and recreation activity?

96484.sol:
Robert Constanza and his colleagues have very recently tried to put price tags on nature’s life-support services. Researchers have put an average price tag of USD 33 trillion a year on these fundamental ecosystem services, which are largely taken for granted because they are free. This is near twice the value of the global gross national product GNP which is USD 18 trillion.

Out of the total cost of various ecosystem services, the soil formation accounts for about 50%, and contributions of other services like recreation and nutrient cycling, are less than 10% each. The cost of climate regulation and habitat for wildlife is about 6% each.

97250.subject: Botany
97250.text:
Read the statements about ethylene given below and select the statements that are correct.

a. Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR.
b. Ethylene breaks seed & bud dormancy.
c. Ethylene is used to initiate flowering.
d. Ethylene promotes root growth & root hair formation.
options: b, c, and d are correct
a, b, c, and d are correct
97250.sol: Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR. Ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially of leaves and flowers. Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during the ripening of the fruits. This rise in the rate of respiration is called respiratory climactic. Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds, sprouting of potato tubers. Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deepwater rice plants. It helps leaves/ upper parts of the shoot to remain above water. Ethylene also promotes root growth and root hair formation, thus helping the plants to increase their absorption surface. Ethylene is used to initiate flowering and for synchronizing fruit-set in pineapples. It also induces flowering in mango.

100415.text:
If we throw a body upwards with velocity of $4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, at what height does its kinetic energy reduce to half of the initial value?
(Take $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ )
100415.sol:
Key Idea : At a given height the half of the kinetic energy of the body is equal to its potential energy. Initial kinetic energy of the body
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} m v^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} m(4)^2=8 m\end{aligned}$
Let at height $h$, the kinetic energy reduces to half, ie, it becomes 4 m . It is also equal to potential energy. Hence,
$m g h=4 \mathrm{~m}
or h=\frac{4}{g}=\frac{4}{10}=0.4 \mathrm{~m}$

100502.subject: Physics
100502.text: Two projectiles are fired from the ground with the same initial speed $u$. One is fired at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, and the other is fired at an angle $(90^\circ - \theta)$ with the horizontal. The sum of their maximum heights is:
100502.sol:
The maximum height of a projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$.

For the first projectile fired at an angle $\theta$:
$H_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$

For the second projectile fired at an angle $(90^\circ - \theta)$:
$H_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2(90^\circ - \theta)}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2 \cos^2\theta}{2g}$

The sum of their maximum heights is:
$H_1 + H_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} + \dfrac{u^2 \cos^2\theta}{2g}$

$H_1 + H_2 = \dfrac{u^2}{2g} (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, we get:
$H_1 + H_2 = \dfrac{u^2}{2g}$

Answer: $\dfrac{u^2}{2g}$

102647.subject: Physics
102647.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If an open organ pipe is dipped vertically in water to exactly half of its physical length, its fundamental frequency will decrease when end correction is considered.

Reason (R): The acoustic length of the resulting closed pipe is exactly half of the acoustic length of the original open pipe.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
102647.sol:
For an open pipe of physical length $L$ and radius $r$, the end correction is $e$ at both ends. The acoustic length is $L_{eq} = L + 2e$.

The fundamental frequency is $f = \dfrac{v}{2(L + 2e)}$.

When dipped in water to half its length, it becomes a closed pipe of physical length $L/2$. The end correction $e$ applies only to the upper open end.

The new acoustic length is $L'_{eq} = \dfrac{L}{2} + e = \dfrac{L + 2e}{2}$. This makes the Reason (R) true.

The new fundamental frequency is $f' = \dfrac{v}{4L'_{eq}} = \dfrac{v}{4 \left( \dfrac{L + 2e}{2} \right)} = \dfrac{v}{2(L + 2e)} = f$.

The fundamental frequency remains unchanged. Thus, the Assertion (A) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

103926.subject: Physics
103926.text: A planar loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic flux linked with the loop is exactly half of the maximum possible magnetic flux that can be linked with it in that field. The angle between the direction of the magnetic field and the plane of the loop is:
103926.sol:
The magnetic flux linked with a loop is given by $\Phi = BA \cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the plane of the loop.

The maximum possible flux is $\Phi_{\text{max}} = BA$ (which occurs when $\theta = 0^\circ$).

Given that the current flux is half of the maximum flux:
$\Phi = \dfrac{1}{2} \Phi_{\text{max}}$
$BA \cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2} BA$
$\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\theta = 60^\circ$

This $\theta$ is the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the loop. The question asks for the angle between the magnetic field and the plane of the loop, which is:
$90^\circ - \theta = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$

Answer: $30^\circ$

107762.subject: Chemistry
107762.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The carbon-carbon double bond in the $\text{C}_2$ molecule consists of one $\sigma$ bond and one $\pi$ bond.
Reason (R): In the molecular orbital configuration of $\text{C}_2$, the $\sigma 2s$ and $\sigma^{*} 2s$ electrons cancel each other's bonding effect, and the highest occupied orbitals are degenerate $\pi 2p_x$ and $\pi 2p_y$ containing four electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
107762.sol:
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{C}_2$ (12 electrons) is:
$\sigma 1s^2 \, \sigma^{*} 1s^2 \, \sigma 2s^2 \, \sigma^{*} 2s^2 \, \pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2$

The bonding contribution of the $\sigma 2s^2$ electrons is cancelled by the antibonding $\sigma^{*} 2s^2$ electrons. The highest occupied molecular orbitals are the degenerate $\pi 2p_x$ and $\pi 2p_y$ orbitals, which contain a total of 4 electrons. Therefore, the bond order is $\dfrac{4 - 0}{2} = 2$, and the double bond in $\text{C}_2$ consists entirely of two $\pi$ bonds without any $\sigma$ bond.

Thus, Assertion (A) is incorrect, while Reason (R) is a correct statement.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

When acetone is added to ethanol, the acetone molecules get between the ethanol molecules and break some of these hydrogen bonds.

Due to the weakening of the attractive forces, the interactions between the unlike molecules (ethanol and acetone) become weaker than those between the like molecules (ethanol-ethanol).

This increases the escaping tendency of the molecules from the liquid phase, resulting in a higher vapour pressure and a positive deviation from Raoult's law.

Answer: Acetone molecules get between ethanol molecules and break some of the existing hydrogen bonds.

114399.subject: Chemistry
114399.text:
Consider the following statements regarding molar conductivity:

Statement A: The value of constant '$A$' in the equation $\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c}$ depends only on temperature and is independent of the type of electrolyte.
Statement B: All electrolytes of a particular type (e.g., 1-1, 2-1) have the same value for '$A$' at a given temperature and solvent.
Statement C: The limiting molar conductivity of weak electrolytes can be obtained by extrapolating the $\Lambda_m$ vs $\sqrt{c}$ plot to zero concentration.
Statement D: Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions is applicable for calculating $\Lambda_m^\circ$ of weak electrolytes.

How many of the above statements are correct?
114399.sol:
Statement A is incorrect because the constant '$A$' depends on the type of electrolyte (i.e., the charges on the cation and anion produced on dissociation).

Statement B is correct. All electrolytes of a particular type (like 1-1, 2-1) have the same value for '$A$' for a given solvent and temperature.

Statement C is incorrect. For weak electrolytes, $\Lambda_m$ increases steeply on dilution, especially near lower concentrations. Therefore, $\Lambda_m^\circ$ cannot be obtained by extrapolation of the $\Lambda_m$ vs $\sqrt{c}$ plot to zero concentration.

Statement D is correct. Kohlrausch's law allows the calculation of $\Lambda_m^\circ$ for weak electrolytes using the known $\Lambda_m^\circ$ values of strong electrolytes.

Thus, two statements (B and D) are correct.

Answer: Two

116330.subject: Chemistry
116330.text:
Match the reactants or stages of the Ostwald process given in List-I with their corresponding catalysts, conditions, or products given in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{O_2}$(I) Recycled $\mathrm{NO}$ gas
(B) $\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2}$(II) $\mathrm{Pt}/\mathrm{Rh}$ gauge catalyst at $500 \mathrm{~K}$
(C) $\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$(III) Concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
(D) Aqueous $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ ($\sim 68\%$ by mass)(IV) $\mathrm{NO_2}$ gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
116330.sol:
The Ostwald process involves the following sequential steps and conditions:

(A) The first step is the catalytic oxidation of ammonia by atmospheric oxygen. This reaction requires a $\mathrm{Pt}/\mathrm{Rh}$ gauge catalyst at $500 \mathrm{~K}$ and $9 \text{ bar}$ pressure. Hence, (A) matches with (II).

(B) The second step is the oxidation of nitric oxide ($\mathrm{NO}$) to nitrogen dioxide ($\mathrm{NO_2}$) gas. Hence, (B) matches with (IV).

(C) The third step is the absorption of $\mathrm{NO_2}$ in water to form aqueous $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and a byproduct, $\mathrm{NO}$ gas, which is recycled. Hence, (C) matches with (I).

(D) The aqueous $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ obtained is concentrated by distillation up to $\sim 68\%$ by mass. Further concentration to $98\%$ is achieved by dehydration using concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$. Hence, (D) matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

119285.subject: Chemistry
119285.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The nucleophilic addition-elimination reactions of aldehydes with ammonia derivatives require carefully controlled mildly acidic conditions.
Reason (R): Mild acid protonates the carbonyl oxygen to increase electrophilicity, but highly acidic conditions protonate the ammonia derivative, destroying its nucleophilicity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
119285.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. The reaction of aldehydes and ketones with ammonia derivatives is acid-catalysed and requires a specific pH range (typically around 3.5) to proceed efficiently.

Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. In a mildly acidic medium, the carbonyl oxygen gets protonated, which increases the electrophilic character of the carbonyl carbon, facilitating the nucleophilic attack by the ammonia derivative. However, if the medium is too acidic (low pH), the basic ammonia derivative itself gets protonated to form its conjugate acid salt (e.g., $\mathrm{R-NH_3^+}$). This removes the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom, completely destroying its nucleophilicity and halting the reaction. Thus, careful pH control is essential.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

119347.text: Equal volumes of three acid solutions of $\mathrm{pH} 3,4$ and 5 are mixed in a vessel. What will be the $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ion concentration in the mixture?
119347.sol:
Let the volume of each acid \(=V\)
\(p H\) of first, second and third acids \(=3,4\) and 5 respectively
\(\left[H^{+}\right]\)of first acid \(\left(M_1\right)=1 \times 10^{-3}\left[\therefore H^{+}=1 \times 10^{-p H}\right]\)
\(\left[H^{+}\right]\)of second acid \(\left(M_2\right)=1 \times 10^{-4}\)
\(\left[H^{+}\right]\)of third acid \(\left(M_3\right)=1 \times 10^{-5}\)
Total \(\left[H^{+}\right]\)concentrated of mixture
$\begin{aligned}
& (M)=\frac{M_1 V_1+M_2 V_2+M_3 V_3}{V_1+V_2+V_3} \\
& =\frac{1 \times 10^3 \times V+1 \times 10^4 \times V+1 \times 10^5 \times V}{V+V+V} \\
& =\frac{1 \times 10^3 \times V(1+0.1+0.01)}{3 V} \\
& =\frac{1.11 \times 10^3}{3}=3.7 \times 10^{-4} M
\end{aligned}\)$

Read the following statements carefully:

Statement I: Deficiency of Vitamin A causes xerophthalmia.

120969.sol:
Statement I is correct: Deficiency of Vitamin A causes xerophthalmia (hardening of the cornea of the eye) and night blindness.

Statement II is correct: Deficiency of Vitamin B$_{1}$ (Thiamine) causes beri beri (loss of appetite, retarded growth).

Statement III is incorrect: Deficiency of Vitamin E causes increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness. Increased blood clotting time is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin K.

Statement IV is incorrect: While most water-soluble vitamins cannot be stored in the body as they are excreted in urine, Vitamin B$_{12}$ is an exception and can be stored in the liver.

Therefore, exactly two statements (I and II) are correct.

Answer: Two

121333.text: What happens to the parental nucleus after the dikaryotic stage?
121333.sol: When a fungus reproduces sexually, two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse. In some fungi the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cells (2n). However, in other fungi (ascomycetes and basidiomycetes), an interveningdikaryotic stage (n + n, i.e., two nuclei per cell) occurs; such a condition is called a dikaryon and the phase is called dikaryophase of fungus. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Later, the parental nuclei fuse </mark> and the cells become diploid. The fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduction division occurs, leading to formation of haploid spores.

121723.subject: Botany
121723.text: Besides starch, what do pyrenoids contain?
121723.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus. The members of chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae. The plant body may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous. They are usually grass green due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b. The pigments are localized in definite chloroplasts. The chloroplasts may be discoid, plate-like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral or ribbon-shaped in different species. Most of the members have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts. <mark>Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch</mark>. Some algae may store food in the form of oil droplets. Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

123523.subject: Botany
123523.text: What is the starting point of all living organisms?
123523.sol: Are you aware that all organisms, even the largest, start their life from a single cell? You may wonder how a single cell then goes on to form such large organisms. Growth and reproduction are characteristics of cells, indeed of all living organisms. All cells reproduce by dividing into two, with each parental cell giving rise to two daughter cells each time they divide. These newly formed daughter cells can themselves grow and divide, giving rise to a new cell population that is formed by the growth and division of a single parental cell and its progeny. In other words, such cycles of growth and division allow a single cell to form a structure consisting of millions of cells.

123874.subject: Botany
123874.text: During the cell cycle, the amount of DNA in a cell doubles from its initial value, but there is no increase in the chromosome number. Which phase of the cell cycle is directly responsible for bringing about this change?
123874.sol:
During the S phase (Synthesis phase) of the cell cycle, DNA replication takes place. This results in the doubling of the amount of DNA per cell (for example, from 2C to 4C).

However, because the newly synthesized sister chromatids remain attached at the centromere, there is no increase in the chromosome number. A cell that had a diploid number of chromosomes (2n) at G$_1$ will still have 2n chromosomes at the end of the S phase.

G$_1$ and G$_2$ are growth phases where DNA content does not double, and Anaphase is characterized by the separation of chromatids, which temporarily doubles the chromosome number in the cell.

Answer: S phase

124070.sol: Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into four types. The metacentric chromosome has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome. The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one longer arm. In case of acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.

124722.subject: Botany
124722.text:
Read the following statements regarding the plant growth regulator that is synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits:

(I) It enhances the respiration rate during the ripening of fruits.
(II) It promotes female flowers in cucumbers, thereby increasing the yield.
(III) It is chemically a derivative of terpenes.
(IV) It promotes horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings.

How many of the above statements are correct?
124722.sol:
The plant growth regulator synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits is ethylene.

Statement (I) is correct: Ethylene enhances the respiration rate during fruit ripening, a phenomenon known as respiratory climactic.

Statement (II) is correct: Ethylene promotes female flowers in cucumbers, which increases the yield.

Statement (III) is incorrect: Ethylene is a simple gaseous plant growth regulator. Gibberellins, not ethylene, are derivatives of terpenes.

Statement (IV) is correct: Ethylene influences the horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening, hastening the ripening of fruits like tomatoes and apples. It is also used to initiate flowering and for synchronising fruit-set in pineapples.

Therefore, 'X' is auxin and 'Y' is ethylene.

Answer: X - Auxin, Y - Ethylene

124907.subject: Botany
124907.text: Which organisms can prepare their own food?
124907.sol: Only green plants and cyanobacteria can prepare their own food; by the process of photosynthesis they trap light energy and convert it into chemical energy that is stored in the bonds of carbohydrates like glucose, sucrose and starch. We must remember that in green plants too, not all cells, tissues and organs photosynthesize; only cells containing chloroplasts, that are most often located in the superficial layers, carry out photosynthesis. Hence, even in green plants all other organs, tissues and cells that are non-green, need food for oxidation. Hence, food has to be translocated to all non- green parts.

125773.subject: Botany
125773.sol: Much before the actual flower is seen on a plant, the decision that the plant is going to flower has taken place. Several hormonal and structural changes are initiated which lead to the differentiation and further development of the floral primordium. Inflorescences are formed which bear the floral buds and then the flowers. In the flower the male and female reproductive structures, the androecium and the gynoecium differentiate and develop. You would recollect that the androecium consists of a whorl of stamens representing the male reproductive organ and the gynoecium represents the female reproductive organ.

125883.subject: Botany
125883.text: Why do flowers produce an enormous amount of pollen in wind pollination?
options: To increase the number of ovules
To counteract uncertainties and loss of pollen grains
To ensure pollen sticks to the stigma
125883.sol: Agents of Pollination: Plants use two abiotic (wind and water) and one biotic (animals) agents to achieve pollination. Majority of plants use biotic agents for pollination. Only a small proportion of plants use abiotic agents .Pollen grains coming in contact with the stigma is a chance factor in both wind and water pollination. To compensate for this uncertainties and associated loss of pollen grains, the flowers produce enormous amount of pollen when compared to the number of ovules available for pollination. Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollinations. Wind pollination also requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents.
125883.meta: Why do flowers produce an enormous amount of pollen in wind pollination?

125914.subject: Botany
125914.text: How does self-incompatibility affect pollen germination?
options: It inhibits pollen germination or pollen tube growth
It synchronizes stigma receptivity with pollen release
125914.sol: Outbreeding Devices: Majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite flowers and pollen grains are likely to come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. In some other species, the anther and stigma are placed at different positions so that the pollen cannot come in contact with the stigma of the same flower. Both these devices prevent autogamy. The third device to prevent inbreeding is self-incompatibility. This is a genetic mechanism and prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil. Another device to prevent self-pollination is the production of unisexual flowers. If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as castor and maize (monoecious), it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy.
125914.meta: How does self-incompatibility affect pollen germination?

126166.subject: Botany
126166.text:
Steps of Artificial HybridisationOrder
A. Bagging1. First
B. Dusting of pollen grains2. Second
C. Rebagging3. Third
D. Emasculation4. Fourth
126166.sol: Artificial hybridisation is one of the major approaches of crop improvement programme. In such crossing experiments it is important to make sure that only the desired pollen grains are used for pollination and the stigma is protected from contamination (from unwanted pollen). Emasculated flowers have to be covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made up of butter paper, to prevent contamination of its stigma with unwanted pollen. This process is called bagging. When the stigma of bagged flower attains receptivity, mature pollen grains collected from anthers of the male parent are dusted on the stigma, and the flowers are rebagged, and the fruits allowed to develop.

127071.subject: Botany
127071.text: Nitrogen oxides produced from the emission of automobiles and power plants, are the source of fine air borne particles which lead to
127071.sol:
Sulfur and nitrogen oxides emitted into the atmosphere react to form compounds that are transported long distances and are subsequently deposited to the Earth's surface in wet and dry forms. Although the term "acid rain" is widely recognized, the dry deposition portion ranges from 20 to 60 percent of total pollutant deposition, and represents the particulate and gaseous forms. A more accurate description of the overall process is acid deposition rather than acid rain.
Dry deposition occurs when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides react, but not with water. It settles out of the atmosphere as particle or gases.
The effects of acid deposition include acidification of lakes and streams, nutrient enrichment of coastal waters and large river basins, soil nutrient depletion and decline of sensitive forests, agricultural crop damage, and impacts on ecosystem biodiversity. Toxic pollutants and metals also can be transported and deposited through atmospheric processes. Both local and long-range emission sources contribute to atmospheric deposition.
